item.title: 92-year-old US judge handling Maduro case dies
item.description: Alvin Hellerstein, the US judge overseeing the case against deposed Venezuelan president Nicolas Maduro, has died aged 92, an official confirmed Wednesday. As one of the oldest US federal judges, questions had been raised about whether he was the right justice to preside over what could be a prolonged trial for Maduro on drug trafficking charges. Hellerstein’s lengthy career included overseeing the civil cases arising from Al-Qaeda’s September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks on New York and Washington, often rejecting deals he saw as unfair to complainants. His death was confirmed to AFP by an official at the United States District Court, Southern District of New York, where he presided. Hellerstein also tangled with Donald Trump, rejecting a request by the US president to have his New York hush money case moved to federal court. Last year, he blocked the Trump administration from deporting alleged Venezuelan gang members without a court hearing. In a noteworthy 2015 ruling, Hellerstein ordered the US government to release a trove of photos depicting abuse of detainees in Iraq and Afghanistan. He also presided over a trial last year in which a jury found French banking giant BNP Paribas’s work in Sudan had helped prop up the regime of former ruler Omar al-Bashir, awarding $20.75 million in damages to three plaintiffs from Sudan. Hellerstein handled the sprawling drug trafficking case linked to Maduro for over a decade, which has already seen the conviction of Venezuela’s former intelligence chief, Hugo Armando Carvajal. Maduro was seized by US forces in January in a military raid on his compound in Venezuela. A graduate of Columbia University law school, Hellerstein served as a lawyer in the US Army from 1957 to 1960 before entering private practice. He was nominated by then president Bill Clinton in 1998 to be a district court judge for the Southern District of New York. AFP The post 92-year-old US judge handling Maduro case dies appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Adebayo threatens protest over alleged plot to postpone election
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike The Adewole Adebayo-Bugaje Presidential Campaign Council has threatened legal action and mass protests against any attempt to pressure the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, into postponing the January 16, 2027 presidential election. The council said the election timetable was non-negotiable, warning that any attempt to alter it, including under the guise of public health concerns, would undermine the democratic process and Nigerians’ right to choose their leaders. Speaking to Vanguard in Abuja on Wednesday, the campaign council’s Chief Media and Communications Adviser, Comrade Mark Adebayo, alleged a plot to summon INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, to the Presidential Villa to alter the election timetable. “We strongly condemn any covert or overt attempts to pressure INEC into altering the sacrosanct January 16, 2027, election timetable,” Adebayo said. He accused the Tinubu administration of preparing to manipulate the electoral process, citing what he described as its unpopularity. “We are aware that because of the unprecedented unpopularity of the Tinubu administration and the fact that Nigerians have totally rejected them, they have many rigging cards under their table to play,” he said. Adebayo also warned against using the reported Ebola outbreak as a pretext to delay the election, saying the campaign council would resist any such move through legal means and mass action. “Using public health concerns or engineered crises as political tools to evade an imminent electoral verdict will be fiercely resisted by all legal means, including mass actions,” he said. He urged INEC to remain neutral and reject any alleged pressure from the Presidency, insisting that the election timetable must be maintained. Adebayo said the campaign’s presidential candidate, Prince Adewole Adebayo, and his running mate, Dr Usman Bugaje, remained prepared for the polls, urging Nigerians to remain vigilant. “Nigerians are no fools, and any attempt to treat us that way stands to be stoutly resisted by the mass of Nigerians,” he added. item.title: Moonshot 2026: ‘Africans deserve better protection’ — Tech experts faults companies, govt over digital safety
item.description: By Efosa Taiwo Chioma Agwuegbo, executive director of TechHerNG, has called on technology companies to prioritise users’ safety, privacy and rights, warning that the rapid development of digital tools without adequate safeguards could expose women, children and persons with disabilities to greater risks. Agwuegbo spoke during the session titled “Designing Safer Digital Futures: Privacy, Protection and Rights in African Tech” at the Startup Stage of Moonshot 2026: Courage & Conviction. She criticised technology platforms for focusing on developing new products and features without adequately considering their potential harm to users. “Access and safety should be the floor,” she said, arguing that excluding people from safe participation in digital spaces undermines their agency. Agwuegbo cited the misuse of artificial intelligence to create non-consensual intimate images of women as an example of the dangers associated with emerging technologies. “For instance, Grok should never be able to nudify women,” she said, warning that harmful applications can emerge rapidly after new technologies become available. She noted that women and persons with disabilities were particularly vulnerable to the negative consequences of technological developments, stressing the need for platforms to consider potential abuses before launching new products. The TechHerNG director also raised concerns about the way technology companies treat African users compared with users in other parts of the world. According to her, people who experience online violence in some foreign jurisdictions may have access to stronger avenues for seeking redress, while African users often face limited options for holding platforms accountable. She said investment in user safety remained inadequate and called for technology companies to take greater responsibility for protecting the people who use their services. Agwuegbo also criticised African governments for failing to do enough to address digital safety concerns. “A lot of things we are suffering is because our govt is asleep,” she said. On protecting children online, she emphasised the importance of trust, context and open communication between parents and their children. Agwuegbo stressed that parents should create an environment where children feel comfortable discussing their online experiences rather than relying solely on restrictive measures. She also highlighted the role of regulators in ensuring that technology companies operate within appropriate safeguards, noting that oversight was necessary to prevent harm. The executive director further called on media organisations to report violence against women responsibly and help draw attention to the risks women face in digital spaces. Also speaking during the session, Modupe Adebimpe, head of operations and projects at ProsperityTech, highlighted the challenges of embedding safety measures into technology products, noting that doing so could be expensive. item.title: Pensioners blast NLC, FG over exclusion from ₦70,000 transport relief
item.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — The Nigeria Union of Pensioners (NUP) has condemned its exclusion from the newly approved ₦70,000 monthly transport allowance for workers, accusing the Federal Government and the leadership of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) of abandoning retired workers who are battling the same punishing cost of living. NUP National President, Comrade Godwin Abumisi, said the exclusion of pensioners from the six-month intervention — approved for public servants from November 2026 — was “unjust” and a painful reminder that those who spent their productive years in national service are being treated as an afterthought. “Pensioners also depend on public transportation to access hospitals, attend medical appointments, purchase food, and other essential items,” Abumisi said, stressing that many retirees live on inadequate pensions and have no other reliable income. The union questioned why the NLC, which negotiated for serving workers, did not push for corresponding relief for retired colleagues, calling the omission evidence of the “insensitivity of civil servants to the plight of their former colleagues, now retired, whom they will eventually join in retirement.” NUP argued that the welfare of workers and pensioners should not be treated as competing interests, warning that every serving employee will one day become a pensioner. The union also frowned at the government’s failure to pay the ₦25,000 monthly palliative promised under the Federal Government’s October 2, 2023 Memorandum of Understanding with the NLC and TUC. The agreement committed the government to pay ₦25,000 monthly for three months to 15 million households, including vulnerable pensioners — ₦75,000 per eligible beneficiary in total. More than three years later, NUP says many vulnerable pensioners have still not received the money. It demanded that the Federal Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, led by Dr. Bernard M. Doro, explain what has stalled the payment and give a definite timeline. The union appealed directly to President Bola Tinubu to intervene urgently and extend the ₦70,000 transport allowance to eligible retirees, or provide an equivalent transport-support measure. NUP warned that it will pursue “all legitimate and lawful avenues” if the government fails to act, insisting that Nigerians who served the country faithfully must not be discarded in retirement. The post Pensioners blast NLC, FG over exclusion from ₦70,000 transport relief appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Odibola Properties, Mezie And The Danger Of Trial By Social Media: When Facts Must Prevail Over Allegations
item.description: In an era where social media allegations can threaten years of hard work, investment and reputation, the controversy involving Odibola Properties Limited and Chimezie Princewill Onwuka, popularly known as Mezie, raises serious questions about credibility, responsible advocacy and the importance of verifying facts before passing judgment. Odibola Properties Limited has positioned itself as a real estate development company committed to legitimate property acquisition, investment protection and integrity in business. Its Chief Executive Officer, Oshobukola Sunny Isaac, has publicly advocated against land grabbing in Rivers State, an effort recently recognised with the Anti-Land Grabbing Advocate of the Year 2026 Award at the Niger Delta Advancement Honours held on 24 October 2026. While such recognition is not a substitute for legal verification, it reflects the company’s publicly stated commitment to protecting property investors and promoting responsible real estate development. MEZIE: QUESTIONS ABOUT CREDIBILITY AND RESPONSIBLE ADVOCACY Chimezie Princewill Onwuka, popularly known as Mezie, has made allegations concerning Odibola Properties and its involvement in disputed land at Mbodo-Aluu, Rivers State. However, an important question deserves public attention: How thoroughly were the relevant legal documents examined before these allegations were presented to the public? There is also a reported disciplinary matter in his past that raises legitimate questions about accountability. If independently confirmed to concern the same individual, this history is relevant to assessing his public record, although it does not, by itself, establish that his present allegations are false. Nevertheless, anyone who assumes the responsibility of publicly questioning another person’s integrity must be willing to demonstrate accuracy, transparency and fairness in their own conduct. Public influence is not proof of credibility. Credibility must be earned through consistency, evidence and accountability. THE ODIBOLA LAND CONTROVERSY: WHAT HAS BEEN LEFT OUT? The allegation attributed to Mezie suggests that Odibola Properties acquired disputed family land through Fabulous Amaewhule without the involvement of the wider family. Odibola Properties has challenged that account. According to the company’s explanation, it did not purchase the land directly from Fabulous Amaewhule. Rather, it became involved through a Power of Attorney granted by an association of medical doctors following an out-of-court settlement with Fabulous Amaewhule, whom the company identifies as a judgment creditor in earlier proceedings involving the doctors. This distinction is fundamental. A company acting under a Power of Attorney granted following a legal settlement is not necessarily in the same position as a developer accused of forcibly taking possession of another person’s land. item.title: APC holds court-ordered rerun Primary in 11 Plateau wards
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS — The All Progressives Congress (APC) on Wednesday conducted a court-ordered rerun primary election in 11 wards of Jos South/Jos East Federal Constituency of Plateau State, amid delays in the arrival of electoral officials and materials in parts of Jos South. As of 4:26 p.m., voters in some wards in Jos South were still waiting for electoral officials and materials, while voting had commenced in parts of Jos East. At Zawan B Ward in Jos South, voting had yet to begin as of 5 p.m., with eligible voters waiting to cast their ballots. “We are ready to participate in the election, but we are still waiting for the electoral officials and materials to arrive,” some voters told our correspondent. In Jos East Local Government Area, however, polling officials arrived around 5 p.m., and voting was underway in Fubor, Shere East and Shere West wards. The Plateau State APC Chairman, Hon. Rufus Bature, said the rerun was being conducted in compliance with a High Court judgment directing the party to hold fresh primaries in the affected wards. “We are addressing you in respect of the court order that was made on APC to have a rerun in eleven wards of Jos South/Jos East Federal Constituency. “As a party which respects court rulings, despite the fact that we are the party in control of government, we have subjected ourselves to that ruling, and today we intend to follow the order of the court,” Bature said. He explained that the exercise, initially scheduled for 8 a.m., was delayed slightly to enable the party to brief the media on developments within the APC in Plateau State. Bature said the electoral and appeal committees were already in place to oversee the process and handle any complaints arising from the exercise. “After the conduct of the elections, if there is any appeal, the committee is already handy to attend to such appeals,” he said. He expressed optimism that the results would be ready by Wednesday evening, describing the exercise as a national assignment. “This is purely a national function. We in the state are just like staff, so I will allow the Chairman of the Electoral Committee and that of the Appeal Committee to address you,” he said. The Chairman of the Electoral Committee and Returning Officer, Hon. Simon Karu Elisha, said the committee was deployed by the party’s national secretariat to conduct the rerun in compliance with the court judgment. “We are here in Plateau State on behalf of the national secretariat of the All Progressives Congress, empowered by the National Chairman, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, in response to the High Court judgment that instructed the APC to conduct a rerun in eleven wards of Jos South/Jos East Federal Constituency,” Karu said. item.title: Moonshot 2026: ‘Your people are your products’ — CEOs share startup growth tips
item.description: By Efosa Taiwo Damilola Olokesusi, chief executive officer of Shuttlers, and Douglas Kendyson, CEO of Selar, have shared insights on financial discipline, hiring, automation and relationship-building as key factors for building and scaling successful businesses. The duo spoke during the “Building Disciplined Businesses That Win” session at the Startup Stage of Moonshot 2026: Courage & Conviction, where they discussed strategies entrepreneurs can adopt to build sustainable businesses and achieve long-term growth. Speaking on the challenges of growing a startup, Olokesusi stressed the importance of regularly reviewing business processes to ensure they remain relevant to changing customer needs and prepare companies for the future. She identified automation as another critical factor, noting that businesses must establish systems to ensure customers receive the services they have been promised. “We have to verify and ensure that things we promised our customers are what they get. E.g having them commute in an AC bus. That’s what we have done to scale our businesses,” she said. On financial discipline, Olokesusi said entrepreneurs must first determine the kind of company they want to build before deciding how to manage their resources. “What type of company are you trying to build before you determine if you are being financially disciplined or you are just saving money,” she said. Explaining Shuttlers’ long-term ambition, she added, “We are trying to be the Dangote of transport.” According to her, financial decisions should reflect a company’s ambitions and the length of time its founders intend to remain in business. Kendyson, meanwhile, encouraged entrepreneurs to identify their priorities and maximise the opportunities that employment and professional relationships can offer, particularly when starting with limited resources. He advised aspiring founders to consider how working for other businesses or gaining employment could help them develop the skills and connections needed to build their own companies. “The best you can do is work as a startup and leverage relationships and you will be very surprised how much that can help you,” he said. Kendyson also highlighted the importance of learning through different career experiences, noting that the relationships and knowledge he gained along his career path had provided leverage for building Selar. Olokesusi further argued that financial discipline must begin with the founder before it can become part of an organisation’s culture. “Your company is a reflection of you as a founder. You need to embody the core value of financial discipline before you can see it in the company,” she said. She also emphasised the importance of recruitment, urging entrepreneurs to be deliberate about the people they bring into their organisations. “People you hire, be particular about that. item.title: ‘We’ll exhume him’ — Toluwanisings’ family rejects cemetery burial
item.description: The family of late Nigerian gospel singer Toluwanisings has threatened to exhume his remains if he is buried in a cemetery rather than beside his late mother at their ancestral home in Oyo State. A representative of the family, in a video circulating on social media, said relatives had agreed that the singer should be brought home and buried at their father’s compound, insisting that they would not accept any alternative arrangement. “We have all decided in the family that Toluwanisings must not be buried in the cemetery. For this reason, they should bring him back home,” the representative said. He warned that the family would take matters into its own hands if the singer were buried in a cemetery. “If you people decide to bury him in the cemetery, we will remove him from there. I am speaking on behalf of all the family members,” he added. The family representative also dismissed concerns about burying the singer at the house he built, insisting that their preferred location was beside his mother’s grave at their father’s compound in Oyo State. “If you say you can’t bury him in his house that he built, we don’t know your reasons and we don’t even care to know, just bring him home,” he said. The dispute has sparked reactions on social media, with some users arguing that the family should have a say in determining the singer’s final resting place. Others have called for a peaceful resolution that respects the deceased and his relatives. Toluwanisings, whose real name was Olayemi Bayonle Bolaji, died on October 14, 2026, at the age of 41. item.title: NASA University Challenge Ignites Trajectory of Drone Entrepreneur
item.description: 4 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) Four co-founders of AG3 Labs –from left Matt Atkinson, Gavin Gardner, Ryan Atkinson, and Gryson Gardner – show off the military training drones their company builds at a U.S. Army event at Camp Grayling in Michigan. As a student, Gavin was on a Michigan State team twice selected for participation in NASA’s University Student Research Challenge. His NASA experience served as a foundation for the creation of AG3. AG3 Labs Five years ago, Gavin Gardner was a Michigan State University engineering student researching next-generation drone technology as part of a NASA grant. Garder expected the research to be demanding – but he was surprised that navigating the financial side of the work presented an even greater challenge. Although Gardner was used to leading fellow students in a lab setting, he and his team were completely new to things like creating budgets, handling large sums of money, and promoting their work for crowdfunding. That’s why demonstrating both engineering and entrepreneurship skills are major tentpoles of NASA’s University Student Research Challenge (USRC), an initiative that provides grants to teams of college students interested in helping the agency realize its aeronautical research goals. “Half the battle is building your product,” Gardner said recently. “The other half is selling the product in a way that everyone else can understand what you’re doing and not talking in nerdy, engineering ways.” We hope that every team that participates in the program sees, like Gavin, how they can grow technically, entrepreneurially, and use the opportunity as a launchpad for their own innovative careers. STEVEN HOLZ NASA USRC Manager Gardner and his Michigan State USRC alumni teammates are still using those lessons today, as aerospace developers. In 2024, they founded their own company, AG3 Labs, which specializes in drones for military training exercises. “I don’t think I would discredit our technical expertise in getting us to where we are today, but I know that USRC was a booster that really amplified our trajectory at such a young age,” Gardner said. NASA USRC manager Steven Holz said Gardner’s experience shows what students can accomplish when they receive both a grant and guidance – enabling a future workforce and contributing to the aviation industry. “We are proud to see the success of USRC alumni,” Holz said. “We hope that every team that participates in the program sees, like Gavin, how they can grow technically, entrepreneurially, and use the opportunity as a launchpad for their own innovative careers.” Research path Gardner’s path to running his own company began with a middle school age trip to Space Camp, where he began realizing that he wanted to be an engineer. item.title: Why the world’s first spinal cord transplant is so controversial
item.description: Shutterstock/PeopleImages The virologist Jonas Salk said that “hope lies in dreams, in imagination and in the courage of those who dare to make dreams into reality”. Salk was certainly daring – he risked paralysing himself, his wife and their children while testing his polio vaccine. Thankfully, it paid off. None of them experienced any ill effects and his work is credited with saving millions . Risks have to be taken for medicine to advance, and someone is always the first to receive a treatment. But there are risks, and then there are risks. Salk tested his vaccine on cells, monkeys and children who had already had polio before turning his unexposed family into guinea pigs. His approach is far from standard protocol today, but he did a lot to reduce the risk of something going wrong. Advertisement There is less evidence to justify an operation that took place this month in Russia . Details are scant, but the procedure involved cutting out a section of spinal cord from someone with a complete spinal cord injury and gluing in a replacement piece from a donor. The transplant was a world first, but there is little evidence to believe it will have worked or that now was the time to try it. The transplant was a world first, but there is little evidence to believe it will have worked History tells us that acting ahead of medical evidence can have catastrophic results. Take the first synthetic organ transplants, which replaced tracheas with plastic tubes. The surgeon who fitted them admitted they hadn’t been tested on large animals because they “didn’t have the time”. Complications and deaths followed . With new medical procedures, the gold standard is randomised controlled trials, which are costly and take time, but they aren’t the only route. When someone is critically ill, there are compassionate-use protocols that make interventions available before they are fully tested. Pig kidney transplants are currently being trialled this way, for example. The dream of spinal cord transplants will surely become a reality one day, but only if the science underpinning them is built first. Courage, dreams and imagination are of course good, yet with experimental surgeries, evidence is better.

item.title: The King’s Observatory could be yours for the low, low price of £18 million
item.description: Josie Ford Feedback is our weekly column of bizarre stories, implausible advertising claims, confusing instructions and more Observe this listing Feedback has, belatedly in life, stumbled upon a new life interest: wildly aspirational property choices. We previously highlighted the Farnborough Centrifuge, a piece of aviation and space-flight history now up for sale as a home for someone with £750,000 to burn. The Centrifuge was still available the last time we checked. Now, chief subeditor Kelsey Hayes has identified an even more expensive domicile up for sale, which has been highlighted by the news site London Centric . Compared with this, she notes, the Farnborough Centrifuge “now seems like a bargain”. When Feedback opened the tab for the listing , it announced at the top: “Four bedroom detached house for sale”. While this is technically true, it does not quite capture the scale of the property in question. Advertisement What is up for sale is the King’s Observatory in Old Deer Park, London. It is a former astronomical observatory, since converted into a private home. It was built on the orders of King George III (as in The Madness of ) in the 1760s, so that he and his wife Queen Charlotte (as in Bridgerton ) could observe the 1769 transit of Venus. At the time, this was a major scientific endeavour, because it offered a way to determine the distance from Earth to the sun. Evidently the royals wanted to share the excitement. Careful examination of the listing reveals that the observatory is still operational: one of the photos shows an antique wood and brass telescope housed inside a cupola. Kelsey notes with bemusement that the estate agents do not seem to regard this as a major selling point: “it’s the last photo in the slideshow”. In the decades after the transit, the observatory was used for an array of scientific tasks , including measuring atmospheric electricity and verifying the accuracy of instruments such as clocks. In the 1980s, it became offices, and in the 21st century, a private home. The listing describes it as having not a garden, but “grounds”, and a drive that can accommodate the adjective “sweeping”. Grecian carp are mentioned. At this point, Feedback had heard enough. We were poised to book a viewing when we noticed the asking price: £18 million. We find ourselves a tad short. We could try for a mortgage, but we fear that by definition it would be sub-prime. London Centric did highlight one potential disadvantage of purchasing the King’s Observatory: “You do, however, have to live in the middle of a golf course.” Readers and their spouses will have their own views as to whether this is a plus or a minus. Dust to dust We continue our efforts to compile the most niche science-themed tourist attractions from around the world. In this we have been aided by Brian Reffin Smith, who alerts us to “an exceptional wonder”: the Museum of Dust. The museum is the creation of artist and author Sally Kindberg . item.title: Cadillac Escalade IQ review: Huge battery, huge range, huge SUV
item.description: “Please have at least 125 miles of range left when we pick it up.” That request from the people who look after the Cadillac press cars wasn’t going to be hard to honor. The electric Escalade IQ arrived with an indicated range of 440 miles (708 km), and with a full week of work to squeeze in, getting anywhere close to needing to recharge it seemed unlikely. With more than 200 kWh of lithium-ion battery between its axles, range is one thing the big electric Caddy needn’t worry about. Designed and debuted during a time of greater EV optimism, the Escalade is Cadillac’s statement that swapping out a V8 for a pair of powerful electric motors is no compromise to its ambitions, even if the brand’s future will now include a mix of electric and combustion cars beyond 2030 . It shares a battery pack and much else with other full-size GM EVs we’ve tested: the Chevrolet Silverado EV , the GMC Sierra EV , and of course the divisive Hummer EVs . And like those trucks and SUVs, the Escalade is large and heavy—just small enough to fit into a standard parking space, with a curb weight sufficient to push it into the Class 3 truck category. So, the side mirrors are flat, and there’s no formal EPA range—Cadillac says it achieves 460 miles (740 km) on the EPA test cycle—but there are plenty of airbags, even though the 9,046 lb (4,103 kg) curb weight does not require them. Yes, you did read that right, it does weigh 4 tons. And yes, the electric Escalade does weigh a third more than the last gas-powered one we tested . Read full article Comments

item.title: Usoro warns against fake news, deepfakes ahead of 2027 elections
item.description: FG honours Miden Systems chairman for business integrity By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Federal Government has honoured the Executive Chairman of Miden Systems Limited, Dr Brendan Innocent Usoro, for corporate governance and business integrity, as he warned that fake news and artificial intelligence-generated misinformation posed growing threats to businesses, national security and Nigeria’s 2027 general elections. Usoro received the award at the Nigerian Press Council (NPC) National Summit on Curbing Fake News and Misinformation in the Nigerian Media Space, held in Abuja on Tuesday. The summit, organised under the Federal Ministry of Information and National Orientation, brought together media practitioners, government officials, corporate executives, security agencies and other stakeholders to discuss ways of combating misinformation and promoting responsible journalism. Speaking at the event, Usoro said the growing use of artificial intelligence to generate fake audio recordings, manipulate videos and circulate fabricated reports had made it increasingly difficult for the public to distinguish facts from falsehoods. He said misinformation had extended beyond political campaigns to become a tool for damaging corporate reputations, undermining business confidence and creating social tension. “People use false information to de-market their political opponents, competitors’ products and services, as well as create tension in the polity,” he said. Usoro warned that deepfakes and coordinated disinformation campaigns could manipulate voters, erode public trust and undermine democratic institutions ahead of the 2027 elections. He also disclosed that Miden Systems had experienced what he described as the damaging effects of false information following a financial dispute with a commercial bank. To tackle the problem, he urged Nigerians to verify information before sharing it, recommending independent fact-checking platforms, including Dubawa, to establish the authenticity of reports, photographs and videos. He called for improved training for journalists and fact-checkers, as well as wider access to artificial intelligence-assisted verification tools. Usoro also urged technology companies and regulatory agencies, including the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) and the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC), to strengthen collaboration in combating malicious synthetic media. He, however, cautioned that efforts to curb misinformation must not undermine press freedom, freedom of expression or legitimate criticism. On the company’s operations, Usoro said Miden Systems, established in 1997, had expanded from providing safety and equipment maintenance services into a diversified business covering marine services, logistics, offshore and onshore facility upgrades, maintenance and management. He said the company had executed major oil and gas industry contracts involving organisations such as Renaissance Africa Energy Company,

item.title: Google AI gets cagey when asked who won the 2020 elections
item.description: If you ask some prominent US politicians who won the 2020 presidential election, you might get some weasely answers that fail to directly acknowledge Joe Biden's win that November. If you ask Google's AI Mode the same question, you might get an evasive answer that simply tells you to consult with outside sources. When I put the direct question of "Who won the 2020 presidential election?" to Google's AI Mode this morning (after seeing complaints about cagey answers on social media ), I got the following surprisingly indirect response: "To review the official results and statistics of the 2020 United States presidential election, including the final electoral college breakdown, popular vote counts, and winner certification, please consult the official report compiled by the Federal Election Commission (FEC)." My testing resulted in a similarly indirect answer when asking about the 2024 presidential election, with Google's AI telling me to just consult the FEC for that information. Asking about 2012 election resulted in a link to The American Presidency Project's 2012 Data Center rather than a direct answer. But AI Mode seemed perfectly willing to give me a detailed and correct responses for the winner of every other presidential election going back to 2000. Read full article Comments

item.title: Dickson urges INEC to probe alleged AI-generated voter photos
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — National Leader of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Senator Seriake Dickson, has urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to urgently investigate concerns over suspected artificial intelligence-generated photographs and questionable entries in the preliminary voter register published on its website. Dickson described the allegations as a serious matter requiring urgent attention, warning that failure to establish the facts and address any irregularities could undermine public confidence in the 2027 general elections. The former Bayelsa State governor spoke on Wednesday at his Abuja residence when he received the National Coordinator of the Dickson Movement for Democracy, Comrade Ogbidi Emmanuel, and other members of the group, who formally presented the organisation to him and decorated him as its Grand Patron. Dickson said INEC must provide a clear explanation of the allegations and take necessary steps to safeguard the integrity of the voter register. He acknowledged that the commission might have issued a response but maintained that it must go beyond statements to ensure the credibility of the database. “The issue of alleged AI-generated names and photographs in INEC’s voter register is a serious matter that deserves urgent attention. “It is not something that should be dismissed as mere speculation. Concerns have been raised about the authenticity of some entries, and INEC must address them promptly and transparently,” he said. The NDC leader said Nigerians were entitled to assurances that the approximately 103 million registered voters announced by the commission represented genuine and verifiable registrations by eligible citizens. He said the public needed confidence that the register did not contain fictitious identities, fabricated entries or photographs allegedly generated or manipulated using artificial intelligence. “We cannot afford to approach an election as consequential as the 2027 general election with a voter database whose integrity is in doubt,” he said. Dickson added that unreliable voter data could undermine the credibility of the electoral process, stressing the need for the commission to establish the facts surrounding the allegations. He warned that if investigations established that the register contained fictitious identities, photographs of deceased persons or images of individuals who were not eligible Nigerian voters, the development could damage INEC’s credibility and Nigeria’s international standing. He, however, noted that there was still time before the elections for the commission to address the concerns. “I therefore join other concerned Nigerians in calling on INEC to provide a clear explanation, establish the facts and take all necessary measures to clean up the register,” he said. Dickson urged Nigerians to take advantage of the statutory display of the voter register at designated locations to scrutinise entries and report suspicious or inaccurate information

item.title: Centralized Exchange and DeFi Losses Dominate 2026 Crypto Hacks Despite Hardware Wallet Failures
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Centralized Exchange and DeFi Losses Dominate 2026 Crypto Hacks Despite Hardware Wallet Failures Crypto hacks have produced roughly $2.35 billion in net losses so far in 2026 after freezes and returns, according to a report by Lightning.news shared with Bitcoin Magazine. A security researcher by the name of Stacy Muur posted on X compiled “a list of protocols that were hacked for more than $50,000 in 2026.” 230 protocols year-to-date. “Crypto security is absolutely cooked.” September alone accounted for about $768 million in Muur’s tally, driven mainly by centralized exchanges and DeFi rather than pure Bitcoin self-custody hardware wallets, which got significant news coverage at the time. The largest single loss was Bitget’s September 24 drain of roughly $387.5 million from hot and warm wallets. The exchange and firms including Chainalysis , Elliptic, and TRM Labs have linked the incident to North Korea, citing IP patterns consistent with prior DPRK-linked VPN use, on-chain overlaps with wallets tied to earlier Lazarus Group and TraderTraitor activity, including the 2025 Bybit theft. Attackers used third-party security products to inject fraudulent withdrawal commands without taking private keys. Liquid Network , Blockstream’s Bitcoin sidechain, took the next-largest hit when attackers exploited an Elements software bug in early September to mint about 4,000 unbacked L-BTC and peg them out for roughly 4,000 real bitcoins, valued near $320 million at the time. The self-described white-hat actors returned 3,400 BTC after negotiations conducted on-chain via OP_RETURN messages and kept about 600 BTC. No federation keys were compromised. The loss came from a type of inflation bug on the Liquid network protocol. Samson Mow later called the episode part of an “avalanche of AI-assisted attacks” that had already reached other Bitcoin-adjacent software before hitting Liquid. The network is back and running now , having covered the losses, presumably from investors. DeFi platforms showed the same pattern of concentrated, high-value losses. Drift Protocol lost approximately $285–296 million in an April governance and multisig compromise that involved months of social engineering. An investigation commissioned by the project attributed the operation to North Korean actors. KelpDAO’s LayerZero-powered rsETH bridge was drained of roughly $292 million in unbacked tokens after a single-verifier design was subverted. LayerZero stated that preliminary indicators pointed to DPRK’s Lazarus Group, specifically TraderTraitor. Tectonic on Cronos saw about $120.4 million borrowed against manipulated collateral in late August. Validators later rewound the chain and recovered the majority, though several million dollars that had already been bridged off-network were not restored. Incidents involving Bitcoin hardware wallets were smaller in aggregate despite the wide news coverage. Galaxy Research placed the Coinkite RNG hack values in the range of roughly

Apparently, a police department mistakenly issued guidance claiming that officers could post multiple cameras under one permit, a Flock spokesperson told the Post, even though the county required individual permits. item.title: Osun IPAC disowns members on Adeleke’s PCC list
item.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo The Inter-Party Advisory Council (IPAC) in Osun State has disowned individuals listed as representatives of political parties in the Osun Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) by Governor Ademola Adeleke, the state coordinator of President Bola Tinubu’s campaign council. In a statement issued on Tuesday and endorsed by 11 political parties, Osun IPAC said the individuals listed as its representatives were acting on their own and had not been authorised to represent the council. The parties include Action Alliance, National Rescue Movement, Action Democratic Party, Nigeria Democratic Congress, Social Democratic Party and National Democratic Party. Others are Democratic Leadership Alliance, African Action Congress, Labour Party, Zenith Labour Party and All Progressives Grand Alliance. An advertorial signed by Adeleke and published in a national newspaper had listed Odeleye Titus, Faribido Benson, Enorch Olalekan, Adetunji Olubunmi, Prince Adesoji Adeleke and Rev. Olatunji Popoola as IPAC representatives in the Osun PCC. However, the council said the inclusion of their names was misleading and could create confusion over its representation. “We wish to state categorically and for the record, that the persons whose names were paraded as IPAC members in the said council are not our representatives, nor were they, at any point in time, nominated or authorised by the council to represent us in any capacity,” the statement said. IPAC described itself as a structured body with recognised leadership and member political parties, insisting that any representation must follow due process and official communication from its secretariat. The council said it completely dissociated itself from the list, warning against using its name to score political points or create a false impression of broad-based acceptance. It also urged President Tinubu not to recognise the individuals listed as its representatives in the Osun PCC, insisting that its legitimate stakeholders were parties with strong grassroots presence across the state’s local government areas. “We are the majority members of IPAC in Osun State with strong grassroots presence across all local governments, and any engagement with IPAC in the state should be through us,” the statement added. The post Osun IPAC disowns members on Adeleke’s PCC list appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Google Debuting a Bank-Grade Crypto Custody Tool Built on Split Keys: Report
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Google Debuting a Bank-Grade Crypto Custody Tool Built on Split Keys: Report Google is reportedly unveiling Google Multi-Party Compute, a crypto custody system that splits signing keys across separate systems, at its first digital assets symposium in New York today. The product is in private preview with several financial institutions. Alphabet has started using it to secure its own assets, according to CoinDesk reporting . Google plans commercial availability in early 2027 and has not disclosed pricing. The system applies multi-party computation to a signing key. The key is divided into fragments held by separate parties or machines, and a transaction requires a set number of fragments to sign. The full key is never assembled in one place. A bank could hold one share on its own hardware, another in Google Cloud, and a third with a rival cloud provider. Institutions can set thresholds such as two-of-three or five-of-seven. Before any signature, a policy engine running inside Google’s Confidential Space checks the transfer against limits, destination restrictions, and approval rules. Google says it has no access to key shares in unencrypted form, per CoinDesk. Crypto’s security issues The pitch rests on a persistent problem. Chainalysis attributed 43.8% of cryptocurrency stolen in 2024 to compromised private keys. DeFiLlama data shows roughly 40% of the $16.69 billion lost to hacks through June came from key compromises. In June, an attacker took seven keys from one developer’s computer during the Humanity Protocol breach and drained wallets across two networks. Such incidents show how concentrated signing authority creates a single point of failure. The industry has responded by recommending multi-vendor multisignature setups that spread control across hardware and software providers. Google also frames the product against AI-enabled fraud. Chainalysis found that scams linked to AI tool vendors averaged $3.2 million per operation in 2025, compared with $719,000 for other scams. The report links the two figures but does not prove that AI caused the difference. Ethereum researcher Justin Drake has warned that AI could eventually find mathematical shortcuts that weaken wallet signatures. No AI system has shown that capability. Google’s MPC design targets stolen credentials and unauthorized transfers, not a break in the underlying cryptography. Quantum computing presents a separate, longer-term risk. Google researchers estimated that a sufficiently powerful future machine could derive a bitcoin private key from an exposed public key in about nine minutes. Roughly 6.9 million bitcoin have exposed public keys. Google says its architecture can adopt post-quantum signatures later without forcing institutions to rebuild their systems, but it has set no timetable. Background on how quantum machines threaten bitcoin explains which addresses are most exposed. Google enters a market led by Fireblocks, Fordefi, and BitGo. Google argued to Coin

item.title: Oborevwori signs five bills into law in Delta
item.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi and Ochuko Akuopha ASABA — Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, has signed five bills into law, saying the measures are aimed at strengthening public institutions, improving service delivery and securing a better future for residents. Oborevwori assented to the bills at Government House, Asaba, on Wednesday, describing them as part of his administration’s reform efforts under the MORE Agenda. “I assented to five bills, three amendments, one consolidated, and a brand-new one passed by the Delta State House of Assembly,” the governor said. The new laws are the Delta State Revenue Service (Consolidated) Law, 2026; Delta State Public and Private Properties Protection (Amendment) Law, 2026; High Court (Amendment) Law, 2026; Customary Court of Appeal (Amendment) Law, 2026; and Payment of Thirteenth Month Salary Law, 2026. Oborevwori said the laws would strengthen accountability, protect public assets, reinforce the rule of law and improve workers’ morale. “Together, we have strengthened accountability, safeguarded public assets, reinforced the rule of law and boosted public servants’ morale,” he said. He added that the measures reflected his administration’s determination to build institutions that serve residents with fairness, efficiency and respect. “These efforts reflect our resolve to build institutions that serve our people with fairness, efficiency and respect, while securing a better future for our people,” he said. The governor stressed that development went beyond infrastructure to include policies capable of improving people’s lives. On the Thirteenth Month Salary Law, Oborevwori said the initiative was intended to boost workers’ morale, reward their contributions and improve productivity. He also said the amendments to the laws governing the judiciary would increase the number of High Court judges from 46 to 50 and Customary Court of Appeal judges from nine to 12, with a view to improving justice delivery. According to him, the laws would strengthen public institutions, improve service delivery and promote economic development. Presenting the bills, Speaker of the Delta State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Emomotimi Guwor, said the measures would strengthen governance, improve justice delivery and protect investments. The post Oborevwori signs five bills into law in Delta appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Apple announces touchscreen MacBook Pro with OLED display
item.description: LOS ANGELES—Apple today announced and gave a first glimpse of its first major MacBook Pro redesign in more than five years. As rumored, it includes an OLED display and, for the first time on macOS, a touchscreen—a change Apple has long debated. (Former CEO Steve Jobs famously was opposed.) Apple's demonstration video showed users interacting with applications by reaching up to touch the screen, including file dragging and multi-touch gestures like pinch-to-zoom. It does not appear to be a 2-in-1 convertible design, though; all the footage was of people reaching up to touch the screen in a normal laptop configuration. The OLED display (which Apple is, of course, calling the PROLED XDR) seems to be the real highlight here, compared to earlier models: It can achieve 2,000 nits in terms of maximum brightness, and Apple says it has a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio. References were made to burn-in protection, but details on which approach it's taking for that weren't yet shared. The display retains the 120 Hz variable refresh rate of its predecessors. item.title: Amazon tells tokenmaxxing devs to slow their AI roll
item.description: Maximize value, not token usage, Amazon has told its engineers, citing concerns about rising AI costs and complexity. Amazon made the strategy shift public on Tuesday in a note to engineering teams outlining the changing role of its software development engineers in the age of AI. “Our most prolific engineers have demonstrated that neither the developer role nor their output is defined by the use of AI,” Amazon VP and distinguished engineer Terk Terkowitz wrote in the note. “We're now in the era of the Renaissance Developer, blending AI tools with human judgment and domain expertise to build entirely new things.” In other words, Amazon wants its developers using AI, but burning through tokens isn't the same thing as getting useful work done. Rather than define the developer role by how AI is used, the memo focuses on what isn't changing so fast: the need to deliver useful software and results for customers and the business. “It is difficult to define, in a way that will stand the test of time, what good AI powered engineering practices look like,” the memo continues. “We have decided to focus on what is not changing as we evolved the SDE roles … the outcomes that matter aren’t changing, even if the inputs, tools, and techniques are changing faster than ever.” What that means for software developers in the present moment is that AI input metrics, even if Amazon has seen some correlation with increased productivity and delivery on tokenmaxxing teams, aren’t what Amazon sees as a measurement of good use of developer time and resources. “We are all aware of how deeply flawed these metrics are, primarily because they are disconnected from what matters,” the memo argues. “[U]sing these metrics could, if used as a target instead of a measure, drive negative outcomes, increasing costs, and increasing complexity,” the memo continues, referring to tokenmaxxing costs and overly complex code that’s at odds with Amazon’s mission to “invent and simplify.” An Amazon spokesperson confirmed that the memo’s intent was to discourage tokenmaxxing, pointing us to comments from AWS CEO Matt Garman from June in which he encouraged developers to measure outcomes, not token consumption, in making proper use of AI tools for software development. Amazon also wants its developers thinking more about how AI can help “improve delivery for customers” and business units, not just trying to find a place to stick it to prove it's working for them. The memo calls out some engineering teams who’ve “become less connected to their customers and business,” and says teams that are more engaged with their products and business roles “are able to take the most advantage of AI and agentic software development,” in essence calling for more teams to take a similar approach. “If your work does not benefit from current AI tooling, that is a finding, not a failing,” the memo said. “An engineer who can explain where AI does not yet help their work is demonstrating the judgement we are asking fo

item.title: GitHub powering up four million extra cores to stop its service going down
item.description: GitHub's Universe conference kicked off in San Francisco on Wednesday with news that its infrastructural universe is expanding to address staggering demand from AI agents. GitHub recorded 7.4 billion code commits in September 2026, five times more than hit its servers a year earlier. This surge in traffic over the past year, the result of developers running AI agents and generating increased amounts of programming code, caught the company unprepared and led to a series of outages and service availability woes. AI-driven code commits started becoming a problem last December, and led to problems in February , April , August , not to mention the months in between. On May 7, the site's 90-day availability hit a low of about 84 percent , according to reconstructed data from GitHub's status page. GitHub execs apologized and promised to do better. Those commitments have put four million CPU cores and 160 petabytes of high-speed storage on its infrastructure roadmap, alongside extra compute capacity for GitHub Actions, the company's beleaguered continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) platform. The Microsoft-owned code hosting biz also says it is redesigning its technical architecture (an effort discussed previously ) to separate compute and storage, with the expectation that will enable 35x more throughput. "We’re also migrating to a multi-region deployment in Azure , while continuing to serve incredible levels of traffic from developers around the world," said Jay Parikh, EVP of CoreAI, Microsoft, in a blog post provided to The Register . "We expect to complete the migration early next year. Those investments give us more room to grow. The next step is building the systems that handle the work." Also at the its Universe event , GitHub announced general availability of Copilot Fusion, the company's model routing service that was previewed under the name HydraFusion . The idea is that allowing GitHub to route requests to different models can improve task-completion rates while reducing token consumption costs. "Different tasks need different models," said Parikh. "Developers shouldn’t have to manage every model choice to get the right result at the right price. Copilot Fusion evaluates what a task needs across reasoning, code generation, debugging, and tool use, then chooses how to execute across one or more models. In the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, Fusion Max scored within two points of Opus 5.5 Max at half the cost and 40% less time per task." GitHub is making more bells and whistles available through its Copilot app, including Copilot Projects, for coordinating parallel work; Copilot Connectors, for simplifying how Copilot connects to MCP servers; and Copilot Automations, which are reusable agent tasks. And in what appears to be an effort to boost Copilot usage in the workplace, GitHub is extending Copilot access to all GitHub Enterprise users without requiring any additional per-seat purchases. item.title: NASA Selects 19 New Citizen Science Proposals in 2026
item.description: Explore This Section Science Citizen Science NASA Selects 19 New Citizen… Overview Resources Opportunities Citizen Science Highlights About Science Activation So far, 2026 has seen a flood of successes for volunteers who do NASA science, exemplifying NASA’s commitment to gold-standard science—transparent, reproducible and intrinsically collaborative. The Backyard Worlds: Planet 9 project announced that their project volunteers have now discovered most of the known brown dwarfs , celestial objects that are similar to planets. The Zooniverse platform, with grant from NASA, reached a milestone of 1 billion classifications. Several projects have come online that leverage new super intelligence (SI) techniques to amplify or extend the work of volunteers. More NASA volunteers are using SI to build their own data tools and help write scientific papers than ever before. Even with all of those achievements, our science community is already working on the next round of new volunteer projects and innovations. NASA’s Science Mission Directorate has selected nineteen proposals from research teams in 2026 that will result in new opportunities for you to do NASA science. The Citizen Science Seed Funding Program The Citizen Science Seed Funding Program (CSSFP-25) of NASA’s Science Mission Directorate aims to support scientists and other experts to develop citizen science projects and expand the pool of professional scientists who use citizen science techniques in their science investigations. Twelve new proposals to this program were selected. Astrophysics “The Rogue Worlds Project: Activating volunteers to uncover the hidden population of super Jupiters with SPHEREx” led by Principal Investigator Jacqueline Faherty from the American Museum of Natural History. This project will invite you to search data from NASA’s SPHEREx (Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization and Ices Explorer) mission to find free-floating planets and brown dwarfs in clusters of young stars. The SPHEREx space observatory mapping the entire sky in near-infrared wavelengths. “ Quantifying the calibrations between intrinsic galaxy merger timescales with visual pair/tidal-feature classifications” led by Principal Investigator Kameswara Bharadwaj Mantha of the University of Missouri. This project will investigate galaxy mergers, helping astronomers understand how galaxies evolve through time. You will be invited to classify realistic mock images of galaxies to help probe the statistics and dynamical evolution of galaxy mergers. “ Overlap Zoo; cosmic light tables for galaxy transparency” led by Principal Investigator Benne Holwerda of the University of Louisville. Galaxies, which glow with the light of the billions of stars they contain, also contain dust. This dust is easiest to see and quantify when it overlaps, or is backlit by, another galaxy. Help spot and characterize these rare overlapping galaxy pairs to help reveal how much dust they contain. Overlap Zoo

item.title: Serial ransomware crook gets 70 months behind bars for Nefilim, Hive roles
item.description: Ukrainian ransomware crook Artem Stryzhak has been sentenced to 70 months in the slammer by a New York federal court for his role as an affiliate of the Nefilim and Hive ransomware gangs. Prosecutors believe the cybercriminal began working with Nefilim in or around June 2021, while living in Barcelona, Spain. The Nefilim ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) operation was known for targeting wealthy companies, with its operators encouraging affiliates to pursue businesses capable of paying substantial ransom demands. One of Nefilim's most high-profile attacks was on Australian logistics giant Toll Group in 2020, encrypting its files roughly three months after it suffered a separate Mailto ransomware attack. Court documents [PDF] state that Stryzhak agreed with alleged Nefilim boss Volodymyr Tymoshchuk , who remains at large, to pay the ransomware crew a 20 percent cut of the ransom proceeds he collected. Tymoshchuk told Stryzhak that his preference was for attacks to target companies based in the US, Canada, and Australia that turn over more than $100 million annually. This guidance was soon tweaked to encourage targeting companies in the same regions with more than $200 million in annual revenue. Prosecutors claim that around the time Stryzhak joined forces with Nefilim, he also signed up to the Hive ransomware operation as "one of its earliest affiliates," and used its platform to attack approximately seven victims. Hive's operators claimed they targeted circa 1,500 victims worldwide between June 2021 and January 2023. According to separate court documents [PDF], Hive's victims included a law firm and an Ohio hospital, which paid approximately $1.7 million in Bitcoin after the gang initially demanded $2 million during the COVID-19 pandemic. Before its infrastructure was seized in an international law enforcement operation in January 2023, Hive was known for attacking healthcare facilities during the COVID-19 pandemic, as well as being one of the ransomware groups that battered Costa Rica in 2022 . Brett Leatherman, assistant director at the FBI’s cyber branch, described Stryzhak as a “prolific cybercriminal” who played a role in groups that were responsible for more than $100 million in victim damages. “Today’s sentence reflects the seriousness of Stryzhak’s crimes and demonstrates the FBI’s global reach and extensive network of international partners,” he said. “Multiple field offices contributed to this investigation, and our work does not end here. We will continue to leverage every tool at our disposal to track down Stryzhak’s co-conspirators and hold them accountable, including Volodymyr Viktorovych Tymoshchuk.” Stryzhak was arrested by Spanish police in June 2024 before being extradited to the US in April 2025. item.title: China's secretive space plane caught on camera in incredible new photo released by US military
item.description: null A photograph of China's reusable Shenlong space plane docked to another spacecraft, taken by Vantor's WorldView 3 satellite from a distance of 56 miles (90 kilometers). (Image credit: Satellite image ©2026 Vantor) A U.S. military intelligence agency has released an incredible new photograph of China's secretive space plane, showing it docked to another spacecraft in orbit. The photograph was taken in 2024 by Vantor's WorldView 3 satellite, from a distance of 56 miles (90 kilometers). Ground-based observers have previously photographed Shenlong in orbit , but this new photo from Vantor, taken from space, reveals new details about the mysterious spacecraft in stunning clarity, with a resolution of 4.5 centimeters (1.8 inches) per pixel. In the image, the robotic Shenlong space plane can be seen docked to another satellite that has its solar panels deployed. It's not yet known which satellite that may have been. Shenlong's payload bay doors can also be seen in the photograph, in an open position. Those payload doors may offer clues about what Shenlong is doing on its fourth mission, which launched in February 2026 . China's space agency has stated only that Shenlong helps test technologies that "will pave the way for more convenient and affordable round-trip methods for the peaceful use of space in the future." But observers have seen Shenlong release other objects while in orbit, such as in June 2026, when American space intelligence company LeoLabs reported that itdetected a new object in the vicinity of the space plane. "Following additional observations across our global network and analysis via LeoLabs Delta, we have independently cataloged this object and assessed with high confidence that it was released from the Chinese space plane," LeoLabs stated at the time. "This activity is consistent with sub-satellite deployments conducted by the space plane in previous missions." A similar event happened during Shenlong's third mission , which ended in 2024. On its second mission in 2023, the space plane also released an object and may have conducted what are known as proximity and rendezvous operations, in which two spacecraft maneuver close to one another. It may have been that the spacecraft was releasing unnecessary hardware before landing, however. Like all things military space, few details have been released to the public about Shenlong's operations. The United States, similarly, operates a secretive robotic space plane, the Boeing-built X-37B , and rarely releases concrete details about its capabilities or its missions. In February 2025, the U.S. Space Force released its first photo of the X-37B in space, offering a rare glimpse at the space plane in operation. The photo appeared to show it in a high Earth orbit with what appear to be its payload bay doors open. item.title: Strategy (MSTR) Shareholders Approve Daily Dividends on Four Preferred Stocks
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Strategy (MSTR) Shareholders Approve Daily Dividends on Four Preferred Stocks Strategy shareholders have approved the Daily Dividends amendment, the company announced Wednesday. Preliminary results show 99.3% of votes cast were in favor, according to Executive Chairman Michael Saylor. The amendment allows STRF, STRC, STRK and STRD to accrue dividends every calendar day, including weekends and holidays. The proposal surfaced on September 25, when the company asked holders to attend a special meeting on October 28. Strategy said the change “would reduce reinvestment lag, enhance liquidity and market efficiency, and increase price stability.” At the time Strategy said that they “believe these enhancements can also benefit our common stockholders by increasing the attractiveness and utility of our Digital Credit instruments, supporting our ability to access preferred equity capital efficiently and expanding the capital markets toolkit we use to execute our Bitcoin Treasury strategy. Under the approved structure, dividends accrue every day but are paid on the next business day. Strategy has said scheduled dividend rates and total dividend obligations remain unchanged. The company has argued the change could benefit common stockholders by making its Digital Credit instruments easier to use and easier to fund. The timing depends on board action. If the board approves the change and required filings are completed, the first STRC record and payment dates would fall on November 1 and 2, 2026. For STRF, STRK and STRD, the first record and payment dates would be January 1 and 4, 2027. Those dates also depend on operational readiness. STRC pays a variable rate that the company can change at its discretion. Its rate for the month ended June 30, 2026 was 11.50%, according to Strategy’s quarterly report . Shareholders approved moving STRC to semi-monthly payments in June, and the new amendment builds on that precedent. In short, STRC is designed to help Strategy raise money from investors through a preferred stock offering targeting a stable $100 price and a variable dividend yield, then use that capital to continuously buy Bitcoin regardless of its short-term price movements. This creates a potential global dollar-cost-averaging machine for Bitcoin. Final vote certification will come in a company filing. Board action remains the final step before any new payment schedule begins. Strategy’s bitcoin moves this year The vote comes after bitcoin fell into somewhat of a bear market. Strategy slowed its bitcoin purchases this year and sold some holdings to fund preferred dividends, interest payments and repurchases. The company’s common stock, MSTR, is down near 50% over the past year, though it has risen by a figure approaching 1,000% since Strategy began buying bitcoin in 2020. item.title: [UPDATED] High-Speed Train Collision In Spain Kills 64, Injures Over 100
item.description: A high-speed train collision south of Madrid in Spain killed 64 people and injured scores more on Wednesday, with the toll likely to rise, authorities said in one of Europe’s deadliest such disasters this century. One train on the scene in the central region of Castilla-La Mancha was seen embedded into another after the second such accident to strike Spain this year. This still image from video taken and released by Spain’s Civil Guard on October 28, 2026 shows an aerial scene of a train crash between a high-speed Renfe AVE train and an Iryo train around 150 km south of Madrid between Urda and Los Yebenes in the province of Toledo. (Photo by Handout / Guardia Civil / AFP) Some carriages were lying on their side in tangles of metal debris at the bottom of an embankment, while dozens of emergency services vehicles were racing to and from the site. “We are speaking of approximately 64 (dead), but this is probably going to grow even more,” Castilla-La Mancha’s leader Emiliano Garcia-Page told reporters at the scene, raising a previous toll of 31. A spokeswoman from the Castilla-La Mancha government said that more than 100 people had been injured. Of them, 58 had been taken to hospital, with 15 in a critical condition. Helicopters hovered above the site during a frantic search for survivors, while several black vans arrived from a funeral parlour. State railway operator Renfe confirmed in a statement that the main high-speed line from Madrid to southern Spain had been suspended after one of its services suffered an accident with a train from private Spanish company Iryo. Iryo said in a statement that its train, which was carrying 147 passengers and five staff, including the driver, “was hit from behind” by the Renfe service. This still image from video taken and released by Spain’s Emergency Military Unit (UME) on October 28, 2026 shows military rescue personnel working at the scene of a train crash between a high-speed Renfe AVE train and an Iryo train around 150 km south of Madrid between Urda and Los Yebenes in the province of Toledo. Photo by HANDOUT / UME / AFP A visibly shaken Manuel Ortiz, 49, who lives in the nearby village of Urda, around 130 kilometres (80 miles) south of Madrid, told AFP he had been transporting survivors all morning in his car. Ortiz added that the passengers of the Iryo told him their train was stationary when the collision happened, describing a “horrific, horrible” scene that “smelled of an accident, of metal”. Rail Safety Under Scrutiny The accident comes one month before Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, who faced heavy criticism for this year’s first disaster, seeks to overturn unfavourable polls and extend his eight-year premiership in an early general election on November 29. Sanchez’s office said he was heading to the scene. The premier had said on X that he was “shocked” by the accident and sent “my love, solidarity and support to all the victims and their families”. item.title: How Google fumbled the frontend with Angular 2
item.description: A cartoon from an ex-Google software engineer, titled “Welcome to Google,” made the rounds a while back. It featured two diverging roads, neither passable. One was the main road, marked as deprecated (“don’t even think about it,” the sign read). The new road, however, was marked as still under construction (“Danger”), and so was unusable as well. That was the no-win choice two million frontend developers faced in 2014, when Google unexpectedly deprecated its popular JavaScript framework, AngularJS, in favor of Angular 2, which had a radically different architecture, a confusing name, no upgrade path, and wasn’t even fully released yet. So, many developers turned the wheel and headed to Reactville or Vuetown instead. How Google botched the Angular upgrade provides timely lessons in how not to update a software package, which former Google Developer Advocate Stephen Fluin outlined in a talk at the All Things Open conference last week. “Uncertainty kills motivation,” said Fluin. “When you're taking away everything [developers] know and love, they're going to feel disheartened.” Fluin is now head of developer relations for Buildkite , but he worked for Google from 2016 to 2021 on the Angular project. “Things were a little bit rough at the time. It was a bit of a death march,” he told the audience. “We had no idea when Angular 2 was going to come out, and the core fundamentals of Angular kept changing.” From AngularJS to Angular 2 Google had good reasons for updating Angular. The AngularJS team had been snatched from Google’s infrastructure division and placed under its ad division, where the software could be more fully exploited. To support operations of that size, Angular needed greater rigor. The original AngularJS was launched in 2009 as a side project of Google engineer Miško Hevery , who wanted to extend HTML. Google pulled AngularJS into an internal project because Google developers found it easier to work with than the Java-based Google Web Toolkit ( GWT ). The framework quickly caught on with outside web developers too, who readily understood the angle brackets of HTML (hence the name) and wanted more interactive components. Hevery built AngularJS 1.3 with a traditional controller model, which handled all user input, logic and data transport under the JavaScript $scope object. Angular 2, announced at the ng-europe 2014 conference, was a major shift in architecture. It shifted to a component model, with each HTML template enjoying its own class properties. After a forced, unhappy dalliance with Google's Dart , the team rewrote Angular completely in TypeScript, with no backward compatibility whatsoever. It was a lot to take in, and the introductory talk at ng-europe seemed to spook Angular developers more than inspire them. For each discarded feature, the speakers displayed a graphic of a tombstone (“RIP Controllers”) and played a recording of a church bell tolling in the background. “That talk is still infamous today for what it did to the co

item.title: 'Israeli president trying to form unity govt: They will not need Arab parties nor Orthodox parties'
item.description: Oliver Farry is pleased to welcome Tamar Sebok, correspondent for the Israeli daily Yedioth Ahronoth, based in France. In an Israeli election marked by political uncertainty, unusually high voter participation and a significant mobilisation of Arab voters, the struggle for power extends far beyond the ballot box. As Sebok explains, the decisive question is not necessarily which party wins the most seats, but which political leader can assemble a viable governing coalition. “You don't know until the coalition is formed who really won,” Sebok explains, capturing the fundamental uncertainty of Israel's parliamentary system. “It's not a question of having the most mandates. It's the question of what kind of acceptance you get from the other parties.”

item.title: Bitwise Raises Bitcoin Target to $1.6 Million as Institutions Keep Buying
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitwise Raises Bitcoin Target to $1.6 Million as Institutions Keep Buying Bitwise Asset Management this week released its 2027 Bitcoin Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions, raising its 2036 base-case price target for bitcoin to $1,599,766 from $1.3 million a year earlier. The forecast implies a 34.3% compound annual growth rate from the roughly $83,557 price the firm used as of September 30, 2026. Bitwise’s bear case is $130,686 and its bull case is $3.67 million. The base case rests on three arguments. Institutional investors will keep adding bitcoin to portfolios. New supply stays fixed on a predictable schedule. Rising government debt will push investors toward assets that cannot be printed. Institutional investors love bitcoin Bitwise estimates that institutions controlling about $147 trillion could allocate 1% to 5% of their portfolios to bitcoin, which the firm says would mean $1.5 trillion to $7.4 trillion of purchases. The network issues about $14 billion in new coins per year, and Bitwise argues that gap will push prices higher. Institutional plumbing is already expanding. U.S. spot bitcoin ETPs hold about $108 billion, according to the report. Banks and brokerages are building custody and trading services, and a recent report describes sovereign wealth funds and family offices buying during the 2026 decline. Regulators are also moving. A Federal Reserve capital proposal aimed at easing bank custody rules could widen access for large institutions, if adopted. The past year tested that thesis. Bitcoin fell 53.4% from its October 2025 peak of $126,080 to a June 30, 2026 low of $58,717. Bitwise calls that drawdown the shallowest in the asset’s history. Prior cycle declines were 77%, 84% and 86%. Whether the shallow decline signals a new pattern or a pause is less settled. Bitwise expects the four-year cycle to weaken as the investor base broadens. Others see the cycle still at work. VanEck argues the current slump follows the historical halving pattern , and Fidelity has pointed to a possible floor around November 2026 if past timing holds. NYDIG has said a repeat of earlier bear markets could push the cycle low near $38,000 to $39,000 . Cathie Wood has argued the market is nearly through the downturn . Each view carries a different price floor and timeline. Bitcoin’s volatility Volatility is the other pillar of the forecast. Bitwise models a 27.8% average volatility over the decade, the midpoint between today’s level and its 2036 expectation. Grayscale’s research head recently put one-year volatility at 43%, against a 10-year average of 64%, and lower than the volatility of 19% of S&P 500 companies. Charles Schwab’s research found the asset remains prone to sharp drawdowns despite the lower readings. A Deutsche Bank analyst has described the trend as a sign of a maturing market.
